sections.content: How many people are "teachers of english as a foreign language"?

8,595 people

were counted on the census as "teachers of english as a foreign language" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Teachers of English as a foreign language teach students to speak and write the English language, either for the first time or building on their existing knowledge.

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "teachers of english as a foreign language" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 25 to 29 years. Of the whole working population 11.1% were aged 25 to 29 years. For people working as "teachers of english as a foreign language", 14.7% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "teachers of english as a foreign language" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "teachers of english as a foreign language" included:

  • mechanical engineers
  • financial and accounting technicians
  • newspaper and periodical broadcast journalists and reporters

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "teachers of english as a foreign language" there were more women than men (67% compared with 33%).

This means "teachers of english as a foreign language" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "teaching and other educational professionals".

Men made up 33% and women made up 67% of "teachers of english as a foreign language"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "teachers of english as a foreign language" included:

  • public services associate professionals
  • teaching professionals (other)
  • legal associate professionals

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "teachers of english as a foreign language" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "teachers of english as a foreign language" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "teachers of english as a foreign language", 12.7% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work part-time than full-time (70.3% compared with 29.7%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (59%) than self-employed (41%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
